title: Sections with support in a closed subscheme
statement:
[sk-lem-coefficient-heart] (3) gives a constructible sheaf with coefficients $E$ or $\Qlb$ a
finite filtration whose subquotients are of the form $a_!L$, with $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$
locally closed and $L$ lisse on $S$. To reduce statements about $R\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,-)$
to cohomology on $S$ we use the functor $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ of sections with support in a
closed subscheme $Z$.

Let $X$ be a standing scheme and let $\Lambda$ be admissible. Let $i\colon Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with
open complement $j\colon V\hookrightarrow X$. For a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ let $\underline\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, the sheaf on $Z$ of
sections of $M$ with support in $Z$, and let
$R\underline\Gamma_Z\colon D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be its
right derived functor.

1. $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ is right adjoint to the direct image $i_*$ from
   $D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ to $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, also in the form
   $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A,K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$, and
   $$
   R\underline\Gamma_ZK=i^*\fib\bigl(K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\bigr)\quad\text{in }D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda).
   $$
2. Let $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ with $u\colon S\hookrightarrow Z$ an open immersion,
   and let $L$ be a finite locally projective $\Lambda_S$-module with dual $L^\vee$. Then
   naturally in $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
   $$
   R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)=R\Gamma\bigl(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\bigr).
   $$

proof.text: Apply formal_closed_support_adjunction, the existing realization of det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction for the canonical formal support kernel. Reverse the complementary-range equality. Its normalized ordinary adjunction gives all the adjunction fields and the pointwise Hom-complex formula; substitute the recorded derived-adjunction equalities in its localization triangle. Exactness of the closed direct image is also a consequence of this ordinary adjunction.

source.place: Adjunction, fiber formula, and stratum formula

proof.text: Use openClosedInternalHomFormulas first for the closed immersion i and then for the open stratum v. Construct the complementary closed subscheme by its vanishing ideal. The standing scheme is Noetherian, hence the stratum inclusion is quasi-compact. Specializing first-variable naturality to the identity makes both objectwise formulas natural isomorphisms in K. Identify the two closed support right adjoints by uniqueness of right adjoints.

source.place: Adjunction, fiber formula, and stratum formula

proof.text: On each member of the given pro-etale cover, the finite-free retract is dualizable. Weakly etale pullback commutes with internal Hom, and the covering pullbacks jointly reflect isomorphisms; consequently the canonical internal evaluation for L is invertible globally and L is dualizable. Use the internal dual D=Hom(L,1) to identify ihom L with tensorLeft D. Derive this identification. The derived tensor comparison for single complexes and uniqueness of right adjoints identify derivedHom(L[0],-) with derivedTensor(D[0],-).

source.place: Adjunction, fiber formula, and stratum formula

proof.text: Global sections of a direct image are the global sections on its source. Direct image preserves K-injective complexes because its inverse-image left adjoint is exact, so this identity derives to RΓ after derived direct image. Apply it to the closed and open internal-Hom formulas, use the single-complex comparisons for i_* and v_!, and compose with the dual tensor isomorphism. This yields exactly the stated natural stratum isomorphism using the actual derived global-section functors.
